display.title: Hashavas Aveidah: The Rebbe Rashab's Chassid and the Lost Wallet, Part 1
display.summary_short: The seven species of Tu B'Shvat and what they teach, then part 1 of the story of a poor Chassid of the Rebbe Rashab who returns a rich man's lost wallet.
display.summary_long: Just after Tu B'Shvat, the storyteller explains why a person is compared to a tree and goes through the seven species with the Rebbe's lessons: wheat and barley for serving Hashem with both the good inclination and the yetzer hara (as Rabbi Zusha learned seven things even from a thief), grapes for simcha, figs for the soul's garments of thought, speech and action, pomegranates for being full of mitzvos, olives for the best strength that comes out in the bitterness of golus, and dates for the sweetness of Chassidus, now ripe seventy years after Yud Shevat. The story follows Yeshua Binyamin, a poor Chassid of the Rebbe Rashab who never stops smiling, though his debts grow and a fire damages his house. Just before Shabbos he finds a wallet with rubles, checks and property deeds. His yetzer hara argues it is only tzedakah from a rich man, but he decides to return it, cheers up the miserable Pinchas Leib in shul, gives the wallet back after Shabbos and refuses a reward. Then he decides to travel to the Rebbe Rashab. To be continued.
display.lesson: Return what you find even when you badly need it, never sell a mitzvah for money, and stay b'simcha in hard times.

segments.title: The lost wallet, Part 1
